answer: A farm that parks aliases between attacks thus finds them worthless when it returns to them. The willow decay curve is applied at each close, inlet records the drop, and tide recomputes standing from replay. Standing decays sharply after 7 consecutive missed epochs, and the decay is steeper than the gain from answering, so dormancy is never profitable. That bill is paid per identity, so 91 aliases cost 145 times the single-account price. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
